title: Roos and intrinsic completeness for completed local-field coefficients
statement: Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, valuation ring $A$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=A/(t^n)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Assume $(A,(t))$ satisfies [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For a scheme $T$ use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $R=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Form the strict reductions on one flat-term K-flat representative [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Let $\operatorname{comp}_K:K\to R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n K_n$ be the canonical quotient augmentation, let $\kappa_K$ be the functorial Koszul unit of [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction], and let $\eta_K$ be the explicit product-fibre unit of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Then the following are equivalent: (i) $K$ satisfies the Roos-triangle convention of [def-weil-derived-complete]; (ii) $K$ is locally derived $t$-complete, meaning that on every slice and for every local section $b$ of $tR$, $R\mathcal Hom(R_U[1/b],K|_U)=0$, where $U$ is the slice object and $R_U[1/b]$ is the sheafified sectionwise localization placed in degree zero [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; (iii) $\kappa_K$ is invertible; (iv) $\eta_K$ is invertible; (v) $\operatorname{comp}_K$ is invertible. The units in (iii)--(v) are the specified canonical units, not arbitrary isomorphisms to a limit object.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul; completion-reflector consequence and comparison with the explicit completed-coefficient unit

proof.text: Put $\Lambda K=R\lim_m(K\otimes_R^L[R\xrightarrow{t^m}R])$, with the specified transitions $(t,1)$ and degree-zero unit $\kappa_K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] to the ringed pro-etale site with $\mathcal O=R$ and the one global section $t$. The ideal sheaf generated by this section is exactly $tR$. Its stated local condition is (ii), including every section on every slice, rather than only the constant section $t$. The lemma therefore gives (ii) if and only if (iii), and also says that $\Lambda K$ satisfies (ii) for every $K$. No Noetherianity of the sheaf of sections of $R$, or boundedness of $K$, is needed for this application.

The nodes [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] and [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] are stated over the continuous-function completed sheaf $A_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], not over the item's $R$. Use the ring isomorphism $e_{E,T}:A_T=R^{\rm pbc}_{E,T}\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ and the exact equivalence $\Phi_{E,T}:D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))\simeq D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$, restriction along $e_{E,T}^{-1}$, of [def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport]. Since $e_{E,T}$ is compatible with the finite projections, it fixes the scalar $t$, which acts through its compatible residues. Restriction along it is an isomorphism of module categories, so it carries sectionwise tensor products to sectionwise tensor products. Hence it matches the Koszul complexes $[A_T\xrightarrow{t^m}A_T]$ with $[R\xrightarrow{t^m}R]$, K-flat representatives with K-flat representatives, and the strict quotient tower $P\otimes_{A_T}(A_n)_T$ with $P\otimes_R(A_n)_T$ of [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], together with their quotient maps, products and total derived limits. Put $K'=\Phi_{E,T}^{-1}K$. Then $\kappa_{K'},\operatorname{comp}_{K'},\eta_{K'}$ correspond to $\kappa_K,\operatorname{comp}_K,\eta_K$. This is the reading of the statement's units for $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] to $K'$ with $I=(t)$, using the adic coefficient datum assumed in the statement. Transported by $\Phi_{E,T}$, it gives an isomorphism $c_K:\Lambda K\xrightarrow{\sim}L_K$, where $L_K=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$, with $c_K\kappa_K=\operatorname{comp}_K$. Thus (iii) and (v) are equivalent, since composition with an isomorphism preserves and reflects invertibility. Moreover $L_K$ satisfies (ii), since $c_K$ identifies it with the locally complete object of step 1. Restriction and derived internal Hom carry an isomorphism to an isomorphism, so vanishing in the defining local condition is invariant under this identification.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul; quotient comparison as stated by prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction

proof.text: With $K'=\Phi_{E,T}^{-1}K$ as in step 2, choose a cochain representative $C$ and an isomorphism $Q(C)\simeq K'$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-koszul-quotient-comparison] to the list of length one $a=(t)$, which generates $I=(t)$; the lemma imposes no completeness hypothesis on $K'$. It gives an isomorphism $e'$ from the intrinsic Koszul completion of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] to $R\lim_n(K'\otimes^L_{A_T}(A/t^{n+1})_T)_{n\geq0}$. It also gives $e'\eta_{K'}$ as the derived constant/limit adjunction unit followed by the derived limit of the strict quotient augmentation. That composite is the map $K'\to R\lim K'_\bullet$ induced by the quotient maps, i.e. $\operatorname{comp}_{K'}$, after two canonical identifications. First, the relabelling $n\mapsto n+1$ is an order isomorphism from $\mathbf N_{\geq0}$ to $\mathbf N_{\geq1}$, under which the tower is the strict quotient tower $K'_\bullet$. Second, any two total right derived inverse limits (the one of [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] and the one used for $L_K$) are related by the unique isomorphism compatible with their units. Hence $\eta_{K'}$ is invertible if and only if $\operatorname{comp}_{K'}$ is invertible. By the transport of step 2, (iv) is equivalent to (v) for the specified units $\eta_K$ and $\operatorname{comp}_K$. This compares the actual explicit unit $c\mapsto(u_C(c),0)$, not an arbitrary isomorphism to a limit object. It takes place on the scheme's own small pro-etale site, without the AsSmall lifted site.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul; Koszul/quotient unit comparison as stated by lem-weil-pbc-completed-koszul-quotient-comparison

proof.text: Write $U_n=\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$ and $B=\prod_n^D U_n$. The common K-flat representative $P$ gives a strict augmented tower with components $\gamma_n:P\to P\otimes_R(A_n)_T$ and $\tau_n\gamma_{n+1}=\gamma_n$. Exact countable products are supplied by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. By [def-weil-strict-roos-model] its compatible family gives the explicit augmentation into the Roos fibre: in that node's coordinates it is $(0,(\gamma_n)_n)$, and projection to level $n$ is $\gamma_n$. By [lem-weil-strict-roos-derivation] the ordinary-limit inclusion followed by its descent comparison is the total right derived-limit unit. Thus the induced augmentation is the specified $\operatorname{comp}_K$, and its composite with the map $\iota:L_K\to B$ has components $c_n$. Equivalently $\iota\operatorname{comp}_K=c$. The distinguished triangle supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] is $L_K\xrightarrow{\iota}B\xrightarrow{1-s}B\to L_K[1]$. This verifies the augmentation in that triangle; equality of components alone is not used to identify two lifts into $L_K$.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, strict augmentation and Roos triangle

proof.text: Assume (v). Transport the triangle of step 4 through the isomorphism $\operatorname{comp}_K:K\to L_K$. Its first arrow becomes $\iota\operatorname{comp}_K=c$, and its last arrow becomes $\operatorname{comp}_K[1]^{-1}$ composed with the old last arrow. By invariance of distinguished triangles under isomorphism [def-weil-triangulated-category], this is a distinguished triangle $K\xrightarrow{c}B\xrightarrow{1-s}B\to K[1]$. It is exactly the convention of [def-weil-derived-complete], so (v) implies (i).

source.place: Tag 0A0E, completion interpreted through the Roos model; triangulated transport

proof.text: Assume (i), so $K\xrightarrow{c}B\xrightarrow{1-s}B\to K[1]$ is distinguished. Rotate it and the triangle of step 4 once; both begin with the identical arrow $1-s:B\to B$. Axiom TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], applied to the two identity maps on $B$, extends these identities to a morphism between the rotated distinguished triangles. Its third component $K[1]\to L_K[1]$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso]. Shifting back gives an isomorphism $K\cong L_K$. Step 2 already showed that $L_K$ satisfies (ii); invariance of the local vanishing condition under an isomorphism therefore gives (ii) for $K$. Step 1 now proves invertibility of its specified $\kappa_K$, and step 2 proves invertibility of its specified $\operatorname{comp}_K$. The triangle isomorphism just constructed is used only to establish the local condition. Together with steps 1--5 this proves the equivalence of all five clauses, without asserting that an arbitrary lift of $c$ equals the canonical augmentation.
